q: Spring A is stiffer than spring B. Which spring has the steeper $(x, F_\text{v})$ graph, and why?
a: Spring A's. The gradient of the graph is the spring constant $k$, and stretching a stiffer spring the same distance needs a larger force, so its line rises more steeply.

q: A spring whose spring constant is $200\,\text{N/m}$ is first compressed $0.10\,\text{m}$ and then stretched $0.10\,\text{m}$. In which situation is more elastic potential energy stored in it?
a: The energy is the same, $E_\text{p} = \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 200\,\tfrac{\text{N}}{\text{m}}\cdot(0.10\,\text{m})^2 = 1.0\,\text{J}$ in both, because the displacement is squared and its sign does not matter. The direction of the force, on the other hand, is opposite.

q: A hand stretches a spring. Which two forces form a Newton's third law pair here, and which objects do they act on?
a: The force of the hand on the spring, that is the force stretching the spring $\overline{F}_\text{v}$, acts on the spring, and the force of the spring on the hand $\overline{F}$ acts on the hand. They are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, but because they act on different objects, they do not cancel each other.
